verification_note: block-delimiter support is NOT uniform: while and closures accept a literal `do ... end` as an alternative to `{ ... }`; if does NOT have a `do` form at all -- its alternative to `{ }` is a DIFFERENT Ruby-style `if cond then ... end` (confirmed: `if true do ... end` is a PARSE ERROR -- 'Start the if block with {'; `if true then ... end` works). Do not assume do/end is a universal substitute for `{ }` across every construct.
